name: Milky Way Galaxy
description: The Milky Way is a barred spiral galaxy that contains our Solar System, along with an estimated 100 to 400 billion other stars. From Earth, it appears as a band of light stretching across the night sky. At its core lies Sagittarius A*, a supermassive black hole.
funFacts: The Solar System takes about 230 million years to complete one full orbit around the galactic center (a 'Galactic Year').
The galaxy is constantly moving through space at about 600 kilometers per second.
It has a warped shape caused by gravitational interactions with its satellite galaxies, the Magellanic Clouds.

banglaTranslation.name: মিল্কিওয়ে গ্যালাক্সি (Milky Way Galaxy)
banglaTranslation.description: মিল্কিওয়ে হলো একটি দণ্ডযুক্ত সর্পিল গ্যালাক্সি যা আমাদের সৌরজগৎকে ধারণ করে। এর কেন্দ্রে স্যাজিটেরিয়াস এ* নামের একটি সুপারম্যাসিভ ব্ল্যাক হোল রয়েছে।
funFacts: আমাদের সৌরজগৎ ছায়াপথের কেন্দ্রের চারপাশ দিয়ে একবার ঘুরে আসতে প্রায় ২৩০ মিলিয়ন বছর সময় নেয়।
গ্যালাক্সিটি অনবরত প্রতি সেকেন্ডে প্রায় ১০০ কিলোমিটার বেগে স্থান পরিবর্তন করছে।

quizzes.question: What type of galaxy is the Milky Way?
quizzes.explanation: The Milky Way is classified as a Barred Spiral Galaxy, with a central bar-shaped star structure.

name: Andromeda Galaxy (M31)
description: Andromeda is the closest major spiral galaxy to the Milky Way and the largest in our Local Group. Andromeda and the Milky Way are approaching each other and will merge in ~4.5 billion years.
funFacts: Andromeda contains an estimated 1 trillion stars, over double the Milky Way.
It is approaching the Milky Way at roughly 110 kilometers per second.
Andromeda has a double nucleus indicating it consumed a smaller galaxy in the past.

banglaTranslation.name: অ্যান্ড্রোমিডা গ্যালাক্সি (Andromeda Galaxy - M31)
banglaTranslation.description: অ্যান্ড্রোমিডা আমাদের লোকাল গ্রুপের বৃহত্তম সর্পিল গ্যালাক্সি। এটি প্রায় ৪.৫ বিলিয়ন বছর পর মিল্কিওয়ের সাথে একীভূত হবে।
funFacts: অ্যান্ড্রোমিডাতে প্রায় ১ ট্রিলিয়ন নক্ষত্র রয়েছে।
এটি প্রতি সেকেন্ডে প্রায় ১১০ কিলোমিটার গতিতে এগিয়ে আসছে।

quizzes.question: In approximately how many years are the Milky Way and Andromeda predicted to collide?
quizzes.explanation: Due to gravitational pull, Andromeda and the Milky Way will merge in roughly 4.5 billion years.

name: Sombrero Galaxy (M104)
description: Famous for its resemblance to a Mexican hat with a bright bulbous core and a dark equatorial dust lane. Contains a massive black hole of 1 billion solar masses.
funFacts: The central black hole is 200 times more massive than Sagittarius A*.
Has nearly 2,000 old globular star clusters orbiting its halo.

quizzes.question: What gives the Sombrero Galaxy its hat appearance?
options: Bright stellar bulge and dark equatorial dust lane
quizzes.explanation: A prominent equatorial dark dust lane contrasted against a massive bright bulge creates the hat shape.

name: Whirlpool Galaxy (M51)
description: The quintessential grand design spiral galaxy, featuring clearly defined sweeping arms and a gravitational interaction with smaller companion galaxy NGC 5195.
funFacts: First galaxy recognized as having a spiral structure in 1845.
Gravitational shockwaves trigger massive bursts of new star creation.

quizzes.question: What triggers the high star formation in Whirlpool Galaxy?
quizzes.explanation: Gravitational tides from companion NGC 5195 compress hydrogen gas, triggering starbirth.

name: Triangulum Galaxy (M33)
description: The third-largest galaxy in the Local Group. Features NGC 604, one of the most active stellar nurseries in our cosmic neighborhood.
funFacts: Lacks a central supermassive black hole.
Bound gravitationally to the Andromeda galaxy.

quizzes.question: What major feature is Triangulum missing at its core?
quizzes.explanation: Triangulum lacks a central supermassive black hole.

name: Black Eye Galaxy (M64)
description: Known for a dark band of dust absorbing light in front of its bright core. Its outer gas rotates in the OPPOSITE direction of its inner stars due to an ancient merger.
funFacts: Star formation occurs at the sheer boundary of the opposing gas disks.
Caused by swallowing a gas-rich satellite galaxy 1 billion years ago.

quizzes.question: What unique rotation feature does Black Eye Galaxy possess?
options: Outer gas disk rotates in opposite direction of inner core
quizzes.explanation: Its outer gas sheet counter-rotates relative to the inner core stars.

name: Pinwheel Galaxy (M101)
description: An immense face-on spiral galaxy containing over 1 trillion stars and 3,000 bright H II starbirth regions visible in crisp detail.
funFacts: Nearly double the diameter of the Milky Way.
A famous Type Ia supernova (SN 2023ixf) exploded in its arms in May 2023.

quizzes.question: Why is Pinwheel Galaxy so distinct?
quizzes.explanation: Its face-on angle provides a clear view of its sweeping arms.

name: Cartwheel Galaxy (ESO 350-40)
description: Formed by a violent cosmic collision when a companion galaxy plunged through its core, creating expanding ripples of starburst creation.
funFacts: Outer ring is expanding at 217,000 mph (350,000 km/h).
JWST imaged spoke structures connecting inner and outer rings.

quizzes.question: What created Cartwheel's ring shape?
options: A small galaxy plunged straight through its center
quizzes.explanation: A direct cosmic collision produced expanding density shockwaves forming the ring.

name: Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC)
description: The largest satellite galaxy orbiting the Milky Way. Houses the Tarantula Nebula, the most active star-forming region in the entire Local Group.
funFacts: Orbiting the Milky Way and being tidally disrupted by its gravity.
Contains SN 1987A, the closest observed supernova in modern history.

quizzes.question: What famous nebula resides in the Large Magellanic Cloud?
quizzes.explanation: The Tarantula Nebula (30 Doradus) is an extremely active starbirth region in the LMC.

name: Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC)
description: A dwarf galaxy satellite of the Milky Way containing hundreds of millions of stars. Linked to the LMC by a stream of neutral hydrogen gas called the Magellanic Bridge.
funFacts: Connected to the LMC by the Magellanic Bridge gas stream.
Contains active young star clusters like NGC 346.

quizzes.question: What stream of gas connects the Small and Large Magellanic Clouds?
quizzes.explanation: The Magellanic Bridge is a stream of neutral hydrogen gas stretching between the SMC and LMC.
